editorial:
Imagine a world where the police are too scared to fight the bad guys, but then you have Marion Cobretti. He is the ultimate tough guy cop who does not play by the rules and wears those iconic mirrored sunglasses. You get thrown into a neon-lit city where a creepy cult is killing people for fun. Cobretti has to protect a woman who is the only person left alive to tell the truth about these killers. The whole vibe is pure eighties coolness, filled with leather jackets, big guns, and a lead character who barely says a word but looks awesome doing it.

What really makes this ride fun is the over-the-top action and the way Stallone plays the role of a stone-cold professional. The pacing is steady, though some parts feel a bit slow until the big shootouts start. If you love old-school action movies where the hero never loses, you will love this. It is a total blast if you just want to turn off your brain and watch some bad guys get beaten up.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head in a massive shootout at the cult's headquarters. Cobretti fights his way through the building, taking out the members one by one with his powerful gun. He eventually finds the leader of the cult and has a final showdown. After a tense battle, Cobretti kills the villain and saves the witness. The movie ends with the bad guys gone and the hero walking away, still looking cool as ever.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves eighties action and tough guys.
